name: Priya N.
bio: Priya ran treatment lanes as a 68W and now works 12-hour shifts on a county ambulance. Priya can explain how to get NREMT certified using military training and what the pay cut looks like in year one.

name: Tomas R.
bio: Tomas worked shipboard sick call and a field surgical team before moving into a civilian operating room. Tomas is blunt about which corpsman skills transfer directly and which need a certificate first.

name: Wren D.
bio: Wren moved from Air Force cardiopulmonary work into a hospital respiratory therapy department. Wren went back for an associate degree while still on active duty and can walk through how that was funded.

name: Idris K.
bio: Idris handled patient administration in a combat support hospital and now manages records and coding. Idris is a good person to ask if the clinical roles do not appeal but healthcare still does.

name: Sana P.
bio: Sana ran a shipboard lab and moved into clinical trials coordination. Sana can explain how to talk about protocol discipline in a way that research managers recognise.

name: Della M.
bio: Della built a billing and coding career that survived four moves by going fully remote. Della is the person to talk to about work that travels with you.

name: Riley K.
bio: Riley ran base network operations and moved into civilian cloud infrastructure. Riley used AWS certifications to bridge the gap and can say which ones actually mattered in interviews.

name: Obi A.
bio: Obi maintained tactical networks in the field and now runs a corporate network team. Obi can explain how to translate signal work into language a hiring manager understands.

name: Nadia F.
bio: Nadia moved from shipboard IT into a bank security operations centre. Nadia holds a clearance and can explain when that is worth money and when it is not.

name: Grant B.
bio: Grant went from Marine network operations to running IT for a mid-size manufacturer. Grant is candid that the first civilian job was a step down in title and not in pay.

name: Zoe T.
bio: Zoe operated satellite payloads and moved into a commercial space operations centre. Zoe is one of the few people who can talk about the Space Force to civilian transition first hand.

name: Marcus O.
bio: Marcus supported Coast Guard cutters and shore stations and now leads a support desk for a shipping company. Marcus knows the maritime industry hires Coast Guard veterans readily.

name: Kavi L.
bio: Kavi retrained into software testing specifically because it could be done from anywhere. Kavi can describe the bootcamp route honestly, including what it did not deliver.

name: Reese H.
bio: Reese managed 24-hour maintenance cycles and large asset inventories in the Marines and moved into freight and distribution operations. Reese helps veterans map military projects onto a civilian resume.

name: Jun P.
bio: Jun ran a supply support activity and now forecasts inventory for a retail chain. Jun can explain which logistics software civilian employers actually use.

name: Hollis W.
bio: Hollis ran shipboard storerooms and now manages a distribution centre floor. Hollis started as a shift supervisor and can describe that climb realistically.

name: Ariel S.
bio: Ariel loaded and scheduled air cargo and moved into civilian freight coordination. Ariel can explain how air transportation experience reads to a logistics recruiter.

name: Bo N.
bio: Bo drove convoys and now runs regional routes with a commercial licence. Bo can explain how to convert military driving experience into a CDL without starting over.

name: Freya C.
bio: Freya ran deck operations and small boat crews and now supervises a container terminal. Freya knows the port sector well and where it hires.

name: Cassian V.
bio: Cassian maintained shipboard propulsion and now works on commercial vessel engines. Cassian can explain which Coast Guard endorsements are worth pursuing.

name: Tobin E.
bio: Tobin ran engineer squads on construction and demolition tasks and moved into civilian project management. Tobin can help you describe military projects in terms a construction manager recognises.

name: Imani G.
bio: Imani maintained base utility systems and now manages facilities for a property group. Imani can explain the licensing landscape for trades work by state.

name: Rafe D.
bio: Rafe kept heavy engineer equipment running and now services construction fleets. Rafe is direct that the trade pays well and the hours are long.

name: Lena Q.
bio: Lena operated naval reactors and moved into commercial power generation. Lena can explain the licensing path and why the industry actively recruits from the Navy nuclear pipeline.

name: Soren A.
bio: Soren maintained cutter machinery and now works commercial HVAC. Soren went through an apprenticeship and can say whether it was worth it.

name: Blake V.
bio: Blake flew Army rotary wing and now flies medical evacuation for a civilian air ambulance. Blake can explain the hours and ratings required to make that jump.

name: Devon S.
bio: Devon flew maritime patrol and moved to a regional airline. Devon knows the Restricted ATP rules for military pilots and where the hour requirements bite.

name: Amara J.
bio: Amara maintained airframes and powerplants and now holds an FAA A&P certificate. Amara used the JSAMTCC route and can walk through the paperwork.

name: Nikhil B.
bio: Nikhil worked aircraft avionics and moved into business jet maintenance. Nikhil can explain which civilian shops value military avionics experience most.

name: Teagan M.
bio: Teagan controlled airfield traffic and now coordinates charter flight operations. Teagan is honest about the FAA controller age limits and what to do if you are past them.

name: Wes F.
bio: Wes maintained Coast Guard helicopters and now services civil rotorcraft. Wes can explain how search and rescue maintenance experience reads to civilian employers.

name: Sloane R.
bio: Sloane produced all-source intelligence and now works analysis for a government contractor. Sloane can explain how to describe classified work without saying anything you should not.

name: Emeka T.
bio: Emeka moved from intelligence briefing into commercial data analysis. Emeka argues the briefing skill is the most undervalued thing veterans bring.

name: Yara H.
bio: Yara ran maritime intelligence watch floors and now leads a threat intelligence team at a bank. Yara can explain how clearance transfers work in practice.

name: Callum P.
bio: Callum did geospatial intelligence and moved into commercial mapping. Callum can point at which GIS certifications employers actually check for.

name: Noor S.
bio: Noor conducted interviews and reporting in the Army and now runs internal investigations. Noor can explain how interviewing experience translates outside of law enforcement.

name: Dominic L.
bio: Dominic served as military police and now works municipal patrol. Dominic can walk through academy requirements and what military service does and does not shortcut.

name: Petra Z.
bio: Petra led base security and now manages corporate site security. Petra can explain how to move into the corporate side rather than straight to patrol.

name: Anders K.
bio: Anders did boardings and law enforcement at sea and moved into federal investigation. Anders knows the federal hiring process and veterans preference well.

name: Rosa D.
bio: Rosa moved from Marine military police into retail loss prevention. Rosa is candid that the work is less dramatic and the hours are far better.

name: Kai W.
bio: Kai ran security watches afloat and now supervises site security at a research campus. Kai can explain how to get past the entry-level guard tier quickly.

name: Odalys M.
bio: Odalys ran military pay operations and now manages civilian payroll. Odalys can explain which finance certifications are worth the money.

name: Bennett C.
bio: Bennett handled administration and disbursing afloat and moved into corporate accounting. Bennett finished a degree part time and can describe how that was managed.

name: Simone A.
bio: Simone did Air Force personnel work and now partners with engineering teams on hiring. Simone is a useful person to ask how hiring managers actually read a military resume.

name: Theo R.
bio: Theo managed unit budgets and now administers construction contracts. Theo can explain how procurement experience maps to civilian contracting roles.

name: Halle J.
bio: Halle built a remote bookkeeping practice that moves with the family. Halle can explain how to find employers who genuinely support relocating spouses.

name: Marcus E.
bio: Marcus led infantry squads and moved into county emergency management. Marcus argues that planning under pressure is the most transferable thing infantry offers.

name: Solomon B.
bio: Solomon led Marine rifle squads and now runs operations for an equipment dealer. Solomon can explain how to describe leadership without leaning on rank.

name: Dara V.
bio: Dara moved from infantry into a county fire service. Dara can walk through the testing process and how to prepare for it while still serving.

name: Ilya N.
bio: Ilya moved from cavalry scout work into renewable energy field service. Ilya took a short technical course and can say exactly which one.

name: Quincy F.
bio: Quincy ran unit training and now builds employee training programmes at a software company. Quincy can explain how instructor experience converts to corporate learning roles.

name: Vega C.
bio: Vega analysed orbital activity and moved into commercial space situational awareness. Vega transferred in from the Air Force and can explain how that history reads on a resume.

name: Rune D.
bio: Rune worked launch and range systems and now supports commercial launch testing. Rune can explain which contractors hire Guardians directly.

name: Marisol E.
bio: Marisol coordinates freight remotely and has kept the same employer through two moves. Marisol can explain how to negotiate remote work before you need it.

name: Jonah K.
bio: Jonah moved into compliance work after several stalled job searches at new duty stations. Jonah is realistic about the years it took and what finally worked.

name: Solene B.
bio: Solene ran clinic operations at Coast Guard units and now administers a hospital department. Solene knows the smaller-service transition is lonelier and has advice on that.
